attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: Faithful. The only firm forecast is that both companies will inevitably charge more. The billing shift and subscription cuts are hedged as 'very likely', so they are not scored. No horizon was given.

contract.note: The support condition requires the whole joint outcome, including the hedged billing and subscription parts and proof of the IPO motive. That asks more than his firm commitment, which is only that both will charge more. The contradiction condition and the open-horizon treatment are fair.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own announcement that it plans to take one model out of subscription plans, possibly temporarily. It covers one firm and one model, so it falls short of the early-resolution rule.
OpenAI says subscription prices and quotas are unchanged and some usage now costs fewer credits. Under the contract, a finite period of unchanged prices does not disprove an undated forecast.
The Pro 200 price stays at $200 while its allowances change, but the direction of the change isn't shown. This does not establish a higher comparable charge.

reviews.rationale: The firm part (both firms will charge more) has no deadline, and no conclusive event is in the packet. Anthropic removing one model covers a single firm and may be temporary. OpenAI kept prices unchanged, and its allowance change has no stated direction. The hedged billing and subscription parts are not scored. Unresolved.

semantics.note: A present-tense factual claim. Reading 'demand' as AI compute demand follows from the surrounding passage.

contract.note: Using calendar 2025 is the evaluator's choice, but it is a reasonable completed annual period. Reading 'a few billion' as low single-digit billions is the ordinary meaning. The contract keeps the loss component separate, which is fair.

evidence.note: Epoch's independent estimate gives the two labs' share of operational compute capacity, not annual dollar spending. It casts doubt on the claim but uses a different metric.
A news report of xAI's 2025 AI-segment capital spending of about $12.7B. The contract excludes capex from compute demand, so this is context, though it suggests large spending outside the two labs.

reviews.rationale: Neither item measures 2025 annual compute spending outside OpenAI and Anthropic on the contract's basis. Epoch measures capacity share and the xAI figure is capital spending. Both suggest that outside demand is large, but neither settles it on the contract's metric. The packet also doesn't establish the loss component for both firms on a comparable basis.

semantics.note: A hypothetical with an explicit 'even if' antecedent ($500B a year of combined compute spending). The antecedent is preserved. The affordability aside is a side assertion.

contract.note: The contract keeps the antecedent and treats the condition as unknown. Its reading of 'justify' is the evaluator's, which it flags as such.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional, and no record shows the antecedent ($500B a year of combined compute purchases) has happened. Under policy it is not scored. The packet has no evidence items.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: Faithful to the surrounding passage on spending caps and cost doubts. 'Signs that AI is slowing down' is an interpretive judgment with no defined measure.

contract.note: The speaker gave no measure. The contract substitutes realized industry revenue growth in May 2026 alone, a narrow, evaluator-chosen metric and month. The claim is only that anecdotes are 'signs' of slowing, so this reading is stretched.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own filing shows its quarterly revenue growth accelerating through Q1 2026. It covers one company and a different period from May, so it is counter-context only.

reviews.rationale: 'These are all signs that AI is slowing down' is an interpretive, undefined judgment. The speaker named no metric, period or threshold, and the contract's single-month revenue measure is not a fair ordinary reading. It can't be scored as written. The Anthropic filing is one company's earlier result and would not settle it anyway.
